question:
In the five-sided star shown, the letters \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) and \(E\) are replaced by the numbers \(3,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) \(7,\) and \(9,\) although not necessarily in this order. The sums of the numbers at the ends of the line segments \(AB,\) \(BC,\) \(CD,\) \(DE,\) and \(EA\) form an arithmetic sequence, although not necessarily in this order. What is the middle term of the arithmetic sequence?

[Figure 1](figures/2005_AMC_10A_Q17_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Adding the five segment sums avoids having to determine the placement of every number. Each number is counted exactly twice, because each labeled point is an endpoint of two of the listed segments. Thus the total is
\[
2(3+5+6+7+9)=60.
\]
Let \(m\) be the middle term of the arithmetic sequence and let \(d\geq0\) be its common difference when arranged in increasing order. Its five terms are
\[
m-2d,\quad m-d,\quad m,\quad m+d,\quad m+2d.
\]
Their deviations from \(m\) cancel, so their sum is \(5m\). Therefore
\[
5m=60,\qquad m=12.
\]
The conditions are attainable: assigning \((A,B,C,D,E)=(3,7,6,5,9)\) gives segment sums \(10,13,11,14,12\), which rearrange to \(10,11,12,13,14\). The middle term is therefore \(\boxed{12}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
